picks.excerpt: A report claims SpaceX is internally testing a handheld AI device that would offer a dedicated hardware gateway to xAI's Grok models — Elon Musk publicly called the report 'utterly false', but the rumor adds to the wave of big AI players exploring first-party gadgets.
picks.rationale: User pick 1 — a first-party Grok handheld would open a new front in the AI-device race; Musk's denial itself is part of the story.

picks.excerpt: Project Mirage unveiled Dune, a 50-gram three-button MacBook keypad whose keys change function based on the app in use, offering context-aware shortcuts and AI-powered automation for meetings and productivity apps.
picks.rationale: User pick 2 — context-aware AI macro hardware for the MacBook; the Notebookcheck article on the same product was dropped as a within-pool duplicate (single best source kept).

picks.excerpt: Scientists developed a color-changing tactile sensor that lets robots visualize touch in real time — a step toward more precise robotic manipulation, prosthetics, and surgery.
picks.rationale: User pick 3 — a genuinely novel sensing modality that could reshape robot manipulation, prosthetics, and surgical hardware.

picks.excerpt: Samsung is developing a fingernail-sized storage chip to replace M.2 SSDs in thin devices, promising better battery life and faster on-device AI inference in future laptops and AI PCs.
picks.rationale: User pick 4 — a silicon-level shift aimed squarely at on-device AI inference in the next wave of AI PCs.

picks.excerpt: Ahead of Samsung's July 22 Unpacked, a leak details the Galaxy Watch 9 and Watch Ultra 2: a new Snapdragon chip to power more on-watch AI, plus new health features, watch faces, and a revamped companion app.
picks.rationale: User pick 5 — a fresh, specific leak (health features, watch faces, companion app) distinct from the 07-03 broad Unpacked preview card; new on-watch AI silicon angle.

notes: Notebookcheck Dune keypad article excluded as within-pool duplicate of Digital Trends pick (same product).
